notes: spoken kindly unto thy handmaid is split, kindly to lev and unto to al, since the ASV spends a word on each morpheme (rule 2); the competing reading would fuse al-lev under rule 30, but that rule's one-rendering condition is unmet here.
The ASV's marginal gloss (Hebrew to the heart of) corroborates the idiom and decides nothing (rule 38).

Each ki takes its own for that as one rendering (rule 55). The head is placed on for as the word subordinating the clause; that on the complementizer is the available competing head, named here under rule 8.
